svg.style: --ink: var(--vp-c-text-1, #3d3d3d); --ink-2: var(--vp-c-text-2, #676767); --grid: var(--vp-c-divider, #e2e2e2); --soft: var(--vp-c-gray-1, #dddddd); --surface: var(--vp-c-bg, #ffffff); --orange: #FF7900; font-family: var(--vp-font-family-base, system-ui, -apple-system, 'Segoe UI', sans-serif);
svg.title: Web requests in 2026-09, by kind of device and kind of address
svg.desc: A square mosaic of the requests Cloudflare saw in 2026-09, automated requests set aside, each cell labeled as a percent of those requests. Two columns, on an open device 46.6% and on a closed device 53.4%; within each, requests from a v6 address on top, 29.3% and 48.0% of the column, and from a v4 address below. The v6 cells are orange and the v4 cells gray; the closed column is plain and the open column is striped, so the cell for an open device and a v6 address is striped orange. The two forces act on that cell from two sides: the closed column squeezes it from the right, and the rising v6 share makes it taller, so its area grows only if it gets taller faster than it gets narrower.

text.tspan: Of these requests: how many were made on a device the owner controls, and how many came

svg.text: Open devices, the owner holds root

rect.title: In September 2026, 13.7% of requests were made on an open device, a Windows, macOS, or Linux computer whose owner holds root, and came from a v6 address. That is 29.3% of the requests on open devices. This is the one cell the report is about: a person, an open device, and an address others can reach.

In September 2026, 32.9% of requests were made on an open device, a Windows, macOS, or Linux computer whose owner holds root, and came from a v4 address. That is 70.7% of the requests on open devices. These devices could run a peer, but on this connection they had no routable address to be reached at.

svg.text: Closed devices, the vendor holds root

rect.title: In September 2026, 25.6% of requests were made on a closed device, a phone, tablet, Chromebook, or TV where the vendor holds root, and came from a v6 address. That is 48.0% of the requests on closed devices.

In September 2026, 27.8% of requests were made on a closed device, a phone, tablet, Chromebook, or TV where the vendor holds root, and came from a v4 address. That is 52.0% of the requests on closed devices.

text.tspan: Orange is v6 addresses and gray is v4. Plain cells are closed devices and striped cells are open
devices. Each cell is a percent of the requests people made that month. Automated requests, 36% of
all traffic, are set aside. Source: Cloudflare Radar.
